card.title: We Know the Old Rules
card.instruction: Use an old custom you learned together as the deepest proof of connection, even when the present situation has changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before dinner, we still split the first bread roll. Like when we shared a room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can afford two rolls now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll each have half of two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but you can't buy the sharing separately.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 preserves the first-roll split from shared-room days, A3 adapts it to two affordable rolls, and A5 distinguishes the custom's connection from total food quantity.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's increased means causes A3's half-of-two plan; B4's arithmetic causes A5's sharing-versus-purchase distinction.

relationship.evidence: B2 reasonably notes that scarcity has ended and B4 tests whether the adjusted custom changes the actual amount.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's equivalence to articulate the surviving value of the act; the heightening remains small and relational.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes dinner and an old shared-room bread custom, while B2 explains changed circumstances.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's cannot-buy-sharing line is earned by B4's mathematical reduction, not detached sentiment.
